title: Comparing length and weight
examples: Teacher, how do I know which toy is heavier?
Can we compare the length of these two crayons?
If I put things on the scale, what does it tell me?

explain.say: Put two sticks side by side. Line up the ends. The stick that goes further is longer.
The other stick stops first. That stick is shorter.
Now hold one block in each hand. The heavier block pulls your hand down more.
The other block is lighter. It is easier to hold up.
A balance helps you compare weight. The heavier side goes down. The lighter side goes up.

draw.text: Heavier side down, lighter side up

faq.q: How do I know if something is longer?
faq.a: You can line the two things up next to each other. The one that stretches out more is longer.
No, heavy means it has a lot of weight. A big balloon is still very light.
asks: What is the difference between big and heavy?

faq.q: What does the balance scale show?
faq.a: The scale shows which side has more weight. The side that sinks down is the heavier one.
asks: How do I use the scale?
What does it mean if the scale tips?

faq.q: Can I compare things that are not straight?
faq.a: Yes. Lay a string along the curvy thing. Then pull the string straight and compare it.
asks: Do I have to line them up?

faq.q: If the scale is level, what does that mean?
faq.a: If the scale is level, it means both things weigh exactly the same. They have the same weight.

facts: Longer means something takes up more space in a line.
Shorter means something takes up less space in a line.
Heavier means something has more weight.
Lighter means something has less weight.
A balance scale helps us compare weights.

quiz.say: Look at the two ribbons. Tap the longer ribbon.
quiz.why: The red ribbon goes further. So the red ribbon is longer.

wrong.0: The blue ribbon stops first, so it is shorter.
wrong.2: One ribbon goes further, so they are different lengths.

quiz.say: Look at the balance. Which thing is heavier?
quiz.why: The heavier side goes down. The rock side is down, so the rock is heavier.

wrong.0: The feather side is up, so the feather is lighter.
wrong.1: Things that weigh the same stay level, and this balance is tipped.

quiz.say: Think of a feather and a book. Which word fits the feather?
quiz.why: A feather weighs less than a book. So the feather is lighter.

wrong.0: The book is heavier, because it pulls your hand down more.
wrong.2: The book pulls your hand down more, so they weigh different amounts.
